notes: represents 3: Dark mottled cube with light grey and red blotches on top; looks like an ore or stone block. No visible polygon grid, quads, poles or flagged face. -> Show a light grey cube with a clean dark quad wireframe grid (3x3 on each visible face), one vertex where 5 edges meet highlighted as a red dot (pole) and one face filled red as a bad face (triangle/n-gon).

distinct 5: Dark cube shares form with Section/Clearance blocks and the gridded idea overlaps Remesh's wire sphere on the Refine sheet; the mottled texture is its only difference. -> Use a lighter cube with a crisp quad grid plus a red bad-face triangle so it reads as an inspection report, not a remesh ball or a plain block; optionally add a small check tag/flag beside it like Describe's panel.

legibility 2: At 1x it's a dark noisy cube; the red marks are tiny specks on the top edge and the grid lines are lost in the mottling. -> Lighten the faces, draw grid lines as solid 1px dark lines, and make the red bad face a solid patch at least 3x3 pixels at 1x.

craft 3: Heavy noisy dithering of dark purple, grey and black over every face; random light blotches on top; looks dirty. -> Remove the mottled texture entirely; flat face tones with clean grid lines and one red accent.

represents 2: Cream-topped golden cylinder with drips standing on a dark square plate, one small red mark on top. Reads as a cake, pudding or candle; nothing suggests changing a setting or parameter. -> Replace with a settings object: a slider (dark track with a cream knob and a red value mark), or a dial/knob with a red pointer tick and tick marks around it, sitting on a small grey part to show it acts on an existing feature.

distinct 6: Cream/gold colours differ from Remove (grey bin), Remedy (cream box with red cross) and Fix mesh (grey box with gold key), though cream overlaps Remedy. -> Use a dark-steel dial body with a red pointer so it no longer shares Remedy's cream; avoid gold, which Fix mesh's key uses.

legibility 5: At 1x it's a yellow blob on a dark diamond; the red mark is a 1-2 pixel speck and the dark plate nearly vanishes into the wheel background. -> Make the red pointer/slider mark a bold 2px line; lighten the base so it separates from the dark wheel.

craft 5: Muddy brown/gold dithering on the cylinder sides, drips look like smears, stray light pixels scattered on the dark plate. -> Clean flat shading on the knob/slider, remove the drips and the stray light specks on the base.

represents 4: Grey cube whose top face has a ragged sunken light patch with scattered red/orange blobs and two red nubs on the top corners. Reads as a cracked or melting lid, not as edges/vertices being removed from a surface that stays closed. -> Show a cube top with a clean edge grid where one edge line in the middle is red and drawn as fading/dashed (half present), the two faces either side merged into one smooth patch. Remove the scattered red specks and the corner nubs; keep the top surface flat and closed.

distinct 5: Same grey cube with a red-marked top face as Inset, Extrude faces and Bevel next to it; the corner nubs echo Mesh edit's corner vertices. -> Drop the corner nubs (Mesh edit owns vertex dots) and make the action an edge line vanishing, not a top-face patch; optionally use a flat slab instead of a cube so the silhouette differs from Inset/Loop cut.

legibility 4: At 1x the red marks are 1-2 pixel specks scattered over a light patch; the corner nubs are lone pixels. No single readable red shape. -> Replace the specks with one thick (2px at 1x) red edge line across the top, broken into 2-3 dashes, so it reads as one mark.

craft 5: Outline is solid but the top face is a noisy mix of light grey, dark purple and red pixels; the side faces carry the heavy dot dither. -> Flatten the top face to one clean light grey tone with a single red edge, remove the stray corner bits, and reduce the dot pattern on the sides.

represents 5: Pale pink flattened oval with a few brown squares and one red square. Reads as a cookie, potato or bread roll rather than a patch of skin with pores/freckles. -> Make it a recognisable skin swatch: a flat rounded-square patch (or the back of a hand/cheek bulge) with a fine regular grid of small darker pore dots, a cluster of 4-6 small tan freckles, and one red spot as the accent. Keep the surface flat on top so it reads as surface, not a lump.

distinct 6: Pink colour shared with Flesh (sliced pink block), Blob and Sculpt's pink disc; the oval lump shape is close to Sculpt's. -> Change silhouette away from a lump: a thin square swatch tile, maybe with a magnifier-ring outline over the freckles, so it can't be read as Flesh's block or Sculpt's mound.

legibility 6: Oval silhouette reads at 1x; the brown and red spots survive as 1-2 pixel dots but the pores are invisible. -> Enlarge freckles to 2x2 at 1x and put them in a tight cluster; make the red spot 2x2 and centred so the accent is clear.

craft 7: Clean outline and smooth pink shading; the lower half has a slightly checkered dither and spots are placed randomly. -> Smooth the lower-half dither into flat bands and group the spots deliberately.
